lines.text: 'Why work'st thou mischief in thy pilgrimage,
lines.meaning: Why do you do harm as you travel through the ages, Time?

lines.text: Unless thou couldst return to make amends?
lines.meaning: It would only make sense to do harm if you could come back and repair it, and you cannot.

lines.text: One poor retiring minute in an age
lines.meaning: Just one miserable minute that goes backward (retires) once in an age

lines.text: Would purchase thee a thousand thousand friends,
lines.meaning: would win Time a million (a thousand thousand) friends.
lines.why: Everyone has wished for one minute back, to take back a word or not send the message. Granting that would make Time loved.

lines.text: Lending him wit that to bad debtors lends:
lines.meaning: It would give good sense (wit) to the foolish man who lends money to people who will not repay.
lines.why: There is a play on "lend". Time would lend wit to the man who lends to bad debtors. A minute rewound would let him undo his loan before he made it.

lines.text: O, this dread night, wouldst thou one hour come back,
lines.meaning: If only you would come back one hour on this dreadful night,

lines.text: I could prevent this storm and shun thy wrack!
lines.meaning: then I could stop this storm (the disaster that has struck me) and escape the ruin (wrack) it brings.

summary: Lucrece asks Time why it does harm when it can never undo it, and begs it to give back one hour of this night.
